claims.text: A machine-learning-based potential can improve representation of the many atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
A neural-network potential is a suitable example of the proposed machine-learning-based reference potential.
The intervention is to implement a machine-learning-based potential.
The intervention applies to solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys at high melting temperatures.
Improved representation of atomic configurations produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method is applicable near and above the melting temperatures of the alloys.
Failure to obtain a significant reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
